then.text: Look at that. Not a crisp packet. The puffins have never been so smug.
Come and visit in the summer. Bring a bag. They always do. The puffins, I mean.

else.text: Oh, hello! Mind the nets. I'm clearing the cove. It's mostly crisp packets and the odd oil drum.
The Enclosure's gift shop up the coast sells 'Authentic Welsh Seashells'. They're made in a factory. It's a shame, the real shells are free.

then.text: Not today? That's fine. The tide will be back tomorrow, and so will the crisp packets.

else.text: You spend an hour filling bags. Forty-two crisp packets, one lilo, a shoe and, somehow, a traffic cone.
That's the best the cove has looked in a decade. I'll bake you something. No, really. I've already baked it.
A pair of puffins land on the clean rock and look extremely pleased with themselves.

seal_watcher.text: Grey seals pup on these beaches in autumn. The pups are white and fluffy and look like very cross bath towels.
I came by wading. Splendid, if you like cold. The seals do not judge.

puffin_warden.text: Puffins nest in burrows on Skomer from April. Over forty thousand of them, give or take a few.
I'm a volunteer. I count puffins. They don't stay still. It is a very bad job.

keeper_lh.text: Strumble Head Lighthouse is automatic now. I come for the chat.
The lamp can be seen thirty miles out. The sea has no manners. But I'm very proud of it.

coast_walker.text: Pembrokeshire coast path. 186 miles. I'm on mile 41 and my feet have formed a union.
Britain's only coastal national park, they tell me. Wettest views in Britain.

preseli_farmer.text: Those blue stones at Stonehenge came from these hills. A hundred and forty miles. Pulled, probably, on sleds.
I've a quarry full of them behind the barn. Nobody's asked for one yet.
